title: UpConfig
description:
Top-level `mirrord-up.yaml` configuration.

The file is rendered as a template before parsing: `{{ key }}` inserts the session key, and
`{{ git_branch }}` inserts the current git branch when there is one.

services.description: Per-service configurations keyed by service name.

BodyFilter.description: Currently only JSON body filtering is supported.

oneOf.title: feature.network.incoming.inner_filter.body_filter.json {#feature-network-incoming-inner-body-filter-json}

accept_invalid_certificates.description:
Accept invalid TLS certificates (e.g. self-signed) from the Kubernetes API server. When not
set, the value from the kubeconfig is used.

context.description:
Kube context to use for all services, from your kubeconfig.

A service's own `context` takes precedence, and `mirrord up --context` takes precedence
over both.

operator.description:
Whether to use the mirrord operator. When not set, mirrord tries the operator and continues
without it if that fails.

telemetry.description: Whether mirrord sends telemetry data to MetalBear cloud.

anyOf.title: feature.network.incoming.inner_filter.header_filter {#feature-network-incoming-inner-header-filter}
anyOf.description:
Supports regexes validated by the
[`fancy-regex`](https://docs.rs/fancy-regex/latest/fancy_regex/) crate.

The HTTP traffic feature converts the HTTP headers to `HeaderKey: HeaderValue`,
case-insensitive.

Prefer matching W3C `baggage` or `tracestate` entries such as
`mirrord-session={{ key }}` when you want to isolate one developer session.

anyOf.title: feature.network.incoming.inner_filter.path_filter {#feature-network-incoming-inner-path-filter}
anyOf.description:
Supports regexes validated by the
[`fancy-regex`](https://docs.rs/fancy-regex/latest/fancy_regex/) crate.

Case-insensitive. Tries to find match in the path (without query) and path+query.
If any of the two matches, the request is stolen.

anyOf.title: feature.network.incoming.inner_filter.body_filter {#feature-network-incoming-inner-body-filter}
anyOf.description:
Matches the request based on the contents of its body. Currently only JSON body filtering is
supported.

anyOf.title: feature.network.incoming.inner_filter.header_filter_jq
anyOf.description:
##### {#feature-network-incoming-inner-header-filter-jq}

Supports jq expressions, matches when the expression returns
`true`. The expression is evaluated on each present header in
the request, in `HeaderKey: HeaderValue` format.

LabelTarget.description: Selects every pod in the target namespace that has all configured labels.

labels.description: Exact-match labels used to select pods. All entries must match.

RunConfig.description:
Includes all information necessary to build the `mirrord` command
for this session.

command.description:
The command to run, as a list of the program and its arguments, e.g.
`["npm", "run", "dev"]`.

directory.description:
Working directory for `command`. Relative paths are resolved against the directory that
contains `mirrord-up.yaml`, and the directory must exist.

Only supported with `type` `exec`. When not set, `command` runs in the directory
`mirrord up` was started from.

type.description:
Whether to run `command` with `mirrord exec` or `mirrord container`.

Defaults to `exec`.

RunType.description: Whether the service runs with `mirrord exec` or `mirrord container`.

oneOf.description: Run `command` as a local process with `mirrord exec`.

Run `command` with `mirrord container`. The command must start a container, e.g.
`["docker", "run", "my-image"]`.

ServerlessTarget.description:
Targets a serverless remote workload, i.e. an application running outside Kubernetes with a
`mirrord-agent` companion in each replica, reached through sessions-manager.

- `serverless/{service-name}[/container/{replica-id}]`;

The environment part of the sessions-manager service scope is not part of the target; it is
taken from `target.namespace`, defaulting to `default`.

The `container` field:

Restricts the session to the agent on this replica, as its `ReplicaId` (the agent's
`MIRRORD_REMOTE_SERVICE_REPLICA`, which defaults to the hosting platform's replica id such as
the ECS task ARN, and then to the container hostname). When unset, sessions-manager offers the
eligible agent with the lowest replica id.

serverless.description:
Name of the service in sessions-manager: the logical workload whose replicas
each run an agent companion. Together with the environment it forms the
`ServiceScope` that the session's agent pairing is restricted to.

config_patch.description:
A JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) applied to the mirrord config generated for this service.

Not to be relied upon, `mirrord up` tries to do the right thing by default, so you should
only reach for this when truly needed.

context.description:
Kube context to use for this service, from your kubeconfig.

Takes precedence over `common.context`. `mirrord up --context` takes precedence over both.

default_mode.description:
How incoming traffic and queue messages are shared between the local and the original
service. Defaults to `split`.

`mirrord up --mode` overrides this for every service.

env.description:
Environment variable settings for the local process.

For example:

```yaml
env:
  include: "DATABASE_USER;PUBLIC_*"
  override:
    LOG_LEVEL: debug
```

env_file.description:
Allows for passing environment variables from an env file.

These variables will override environment fetched from the remote target.

exclude.description:
Include the remote environment variables in the local process that are **NOT** specified by
this option.
Variable names can be matched using `*` and `?` where `?` matches exactly one occurrence of
any character and `*` matches arbitrary many (including zero) occurrences of any character.

Some of the variables that are excluded by default:
`PATH`, `HOME`, `HOMEPATH`, `CLASSPATH`, `JAVA_EXE`, `JAVA_HOME`, `PYTHONPATH`.

Can be passed as a list or as a semicolon-delimited string (e.g. `"VAR;OTHER_VAR"`).

include.description:
Include only these remote environment variables in the local process.
Variable names can be matched using `*` and `?` where `?` matches exactly one occurrence of
any character and `*` matches arbitrary many (including zero) occurrences of any character.

Can be passed as a list or as a semicolon-delimited string (e.g. `"VAR;OTHER_VAR"`).

Some environment variables are excluded by default (`PATH` for example), including these
requires specifying them with `include`

load_from_process.description:
Allows for changing the way mirrord loads remote environment variables.
If set, the variables are fetched after the user application is started.

This setting is meant to resolve issues when using mirrord via the IntelliJ plugin on WSL
and the remote environment contains a lot of variables.

mapping.description:
Specify map of patterns that if matched will replace the value according to specification.

*Capture groups are allowed.*

Example:
```json
{
  ".+_TIMEOUT": "10000"
  "LOG_.+_VERBOSITY": "debug"
  "(\w+)_(\d+)": "magic-value"
}
```

Will do the next replacements for environment variables that match:

* `CONNECTION_TIMEOUT: 500` => `CONNECTION_TIMEOUT: 10000`

* `LOG_FILE_VERBOSITY: info` => `LOG_FILE_VERBOSITY: debug`

* `DATA_1234: common-value` => `DATA_1234: magic-value`

override.description:
Allows setting or overriding environment variables (locally) with a custom value.

For example, if the remote pod has an environment variable `REGION=1`, but this is an
undesirable value, it's possible to use `override` to set `REGION=2` (locally) instead.

Environment specified here will also override variables passed via the env file.

unset.description:
Allows unsetting environment variables in the executed process.

This is useful for when some system/user-defined environment like `AWS_PROFILE` make the
application behave as if it's running locally, instead of using the remote settings.
The unsetting happens from extension (if possible)/CLI and when process initializes.
In some cases, such as Go the env might not be able to be modified from the process itself.
This is case insensitive, meaning if you'd put `AWS_PROFILE` it'd unset both `AWS_PROFILE`
and `Aws_Profile` and other variations.

http_filter.description:
HTTP filter that selects which requests reach the local service in `split` and `mirror`
modes.

When not set, requests with a header matching the regex
`baggage: .*mirrord-session={key}.*` are selected, where `{key}` is the session key.
Ignored in `replace` mode. For example:

```yaml
http_filter:
  header_filter: "^x-debug: true$"
```

all_of.description:
An array of HTTP filters.

Each inner filter specifies a header, path, method, body, or jq filter.
Requests must match all of the filters to be stolen.

Cannot be an empty list.

Example:
```json
{
  "all_of": [
    { "header": "^baggage: .*mirrord-session={{ key }}.*$" },
    { "path": "^/api/v1/my-endpoint$" },
    { "method": "POST" }
  ]
}
```

any_of.description:
An array of HTTP filters.

Each inner filter specifies a header, path, method, body, or jq filter.
Requests must match at least one of the filters to be stolen.

Cannot be an empty list.

Example:
```json
{
  "any_of": [
    { "header": "^baggage: .*mirrord-session={{ key }}.*$" },
    { "header": "^tracestate: .*mirrord-session={{ key }}.*$" },
    { "path": "^/api/v1/my-endpoint$" }
  ]
}
```

body_filter.description: Matches the request based on the contents of its body.

header_filter.description:
Supports regexes validated by the
[`fancy-regex`](https://docs.rs/fancy-regex/latest/fancy_regex/) crate.

The HTTP traffic feature converts the HTTP headers to `HeaderKey: HeaderValue`,
case-insensitive.

The recommended pattern is to match a W3C `baggage` or `tracestate` entry such as
`mirrord-session={{ key }}`.

header_filter_jq.description:
Supports jq expressions, matches when the expression returns
`true`. The expression is evaluated on each present header in
the request, in `HeaderKey: HeaderValue` format.

method_filter.description:
Supports standard [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods), and non-standard HTTP methods.

Case-insensitive. If the request method matches the filter, the request is stolen.

path_filter.description:
Supports regexes validated by the
[`fancy-regex`](https://docs.rs/fancy-regex/latest/fancy_regex/) crate.

Case-insensitive. Tries to find match in the path (without query) and path+query.
If any of the two matches, the request is stolen.

ports.description:
Activate the HTTP traffic filter only for these ports. When
absent, filtering will be done for all ports.

ignore_ports.description: Ports whose incoming traffic is not stolen or mirrored.

run.description: How to launch the service's local process.

skip.description:
Don't launch this service unless it is named on the `mirrord up` command line. Defaults to
`false`.

target.description:
The remote workload this service runs against.

- `none`: run targetless.
- A mapping with `path` and/or `namespace`: run against that workload.
- Not set: `mirrord up` looks for a deployment, statefulset, rollout or pod (in that order)
  named after the service.

ServiceMode.description: Incoming traffic mode for a service. Also used as the mode for splitting the service's queues.

oneOf.description:
Incoming traffic is split between the local and the original service using HTTP filtering.

Uses the service's `http_filter` if set. Otherwise, requests with a header matching the
regex `baggage: .*mirrord-session={key}.*` go to the local service, where `{key}` is the
session key.

The local service takes over *all* incoming traffic: the target workload is copied and the
original is scaled down to zero.

The service's `http_filter` is ignored, with a warning. The target must support
`copy_target` with `scale_down`.

Incoming traffic is mirrored to the local service, leaving traffic to the original service
unaltered.

Uses the service's `http_filter` if set. Otherwise, requests with a header matching the
regex `baggage: .*mirrord-session={key}.*` are mirrored, where `{key}` is the session key.

SpecifiedTarget.description: The target workload of a service.

namespace.description: Namespace of the target workload. Defaults to the namespace of the kube context.

path.description:
The workload to target, e.g. `deployment/my-app` or `pod/my-pod/container/my-container`.

When not set, `mirrord up` looks for a deployment, statefulset, rollout or pod (in that
order) named after the service.

anyOf.description: An empty `target`, treated as if it were not set.
